title: Tree-planting drive and Cale88: No link, says OVP
summary: The Office of the Vice President maintained that its nationwide tree-planting program has no connection with Cale88 Foods Corp. after it was raised by the House prosecution team during the…

blocks.text: “The Office of the Vice President categorically denies any association between its ‘Pagbabago: A Million Trees Campaign’ and Cale88 Foods Corporation’s compliance with the Board of Investments (BOI) tree-planting requirement,” the OVP said in a statement.

MANILA, Philippines — The Office of the Vice President (OVP) maintained that its nationwide tree-planting program has no connection with Cale88 Foods Corp. after it was raised by the House prosecution team during the impeachment trial against VP Sara Duterte on Friday.

Prosecution counsel Erwin Matib asked defense witness Trade Undersecretary Ceferino Rodolfo Rodolfo if Duterte’s tree-planting program was connected to a BOI requirement for enterprises to plant at least 100 forest trees to qualify for incentives.

“Any attempt to link the Vice President’s participation in the OVP’s environmental initiatives to Cale88 Foods Corporation’s BOI compliance is misleading, malicious and has no factual basis,” the OVP added.

Rodolfo said Cale88 Foods Corp., the banana chips exporter co-owned by Duterte’s husband Manases Carpio and her dentist Lourdes Lebosada, takes its name from the first two letters of their surnames paired with a number symbolizing infinity.

“The ‘Pagbabago: A Million Trees Campaign” is an independent environmental initiative of the OVP, launched on March 27, 2023 in support of the Department of Environment and Natural Resources’ efforts to reduce carbon emissions and address climate change. The program is part of the OVP’s advocacy to protect the environment for future generations,” the OVP added.
It said the campaign, in partnership with various government agencies and private sectors, has planted 1,386,682 trees nationwide.

“Amid these allegations and political insinuations, the OVP remains steadfast in fulfilling its mandate of delivering efficient, accessible and responsive public service for the good of all Filipinos,” the OVP said.

The firm has drawn scrutiny during Duterte’s impeachment trial after Sen. Risa Hontiveros flagged its foreign remittances – including funds from Chinese entities and a Ukrainian company facing criminal complaints for money laundering and fraud.

Financial forensic expert Alexander Cabrera previously testified that Cale88’s financial statements lacked reported accounts receivable, accounts payable and raw material inventory, despite substantial cash inflows and outflows.

The Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) earlier reported that the firm grossed more than P1 billion at one point and received P776 million in foreign remittances from 2022 to 2025, including P319 million from China.
Duterte should not be onion-skinned regarding the reported link between her tree-planting activities and Calle88 Foods Corp., according to the spokesman of the House prosecution panel.

Lanao del Sur 1st District. Rep. Zia Alontio Adiong said at the Saturday News Forum in Quezon City Duterte seemed to be very sensitive when House prosecutors raised questions on whether photographs of a tree-planting activity which she attended had something to do with the BOI’s tree-planting requirement.
Adiong reminded Duterte that probing questions are part of cross-examinations during regular court trials.
Adiong said prosecutors believe Cale88 is a shell company which earned profits with only two employees, aside from an alleged P319-million financial inflow from China.
The lawmaker said there is nothing wrong if the tree-planting activity is part of Cale88’s compliance requirement with the BOI. — Emmanuel Tupas
